item.title: Nancy Kassebaum Baker, former U.S. senator from Kansas, dies at 94
item.description: Former U.S. Sen. Nancy Kassebaum Baker of Kansas was the first woman elected to the U.S. Senate without following a spouse into office.

item.title: Iran declares it has won the war as U.S. turns to economic warfare
item.description: Iran's president said Friday the world had "approved" the country's victory, as Vice President JD Vance declares economic pressure "the most effective tool that we have."

item.title: Saturday Sessions: Grace Potter performs "Run Baby Run"
item.description: Four-time Grammy nominee Grace Potter returns to "CBS Saturday Morning" to jam out. Her seventh album, "Trespasser," is inspired by road trips from her California home to her native Vermont. Here's Grace Potter with "Run Baby Run."

item.title: Saturday Sessions: Grace Potter sings "Love Me Not"
item.description: Four-time Grammy nominee Grace Potter returns to "CBS Saturday Morning" to jam out. Her seventh album, "Trespasser," is inspired by road trips from her California home to her native Vermont. Here's Grace Potter with "Love Me Not."

item.title: Saturday Sessions: Grace Potter is on "Main Street USA"
item.description: Four-time Grammy nominee Grace Potter returns to "CBS Saturday Morning" to jam out. Her seventh album, "Trespasser," is inspired by road trips from her California home to her native Vermont. Here's Grace Potter with "Main Street USA."

item.title: Chef Philippe Massoud serves elevated Lebanese delicacies at ilili
item.description: Chef Philippe Massoud shares his love of Lebanese cuisine with eager diners at ilili, which has locations in New York City and Washington, D.C. The Beirut-born chef explains how his "enchanted life" and upbringing in Lebanon contributes to his culinary success.

item.title: Harry Potter's golden snitch, Superman's suit and other iconic props up for auction
item.description: Iconic film props and other movie memorabilia from classic Hollywood flicks are up for auction. Kris Van Cleave has more.

item.title: Canada says it will begin retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods after Labor Day
item.description: The U.S. and Canada have wrangled for decades over trade, and somehow, they still managed to remain friends, allies and trading partners.

item.title: Race cars set to zip through Washington, D.C. at the Freedom 250 Grand Prix
item.description: Race car drivers will compete at the IndyCar Freedom 250 Grand Prix in Washington, D.C. this weekend, turning the National Mall into a racetrack.

item.title: Job hopping makes you more adaptable, Jill Schlesinger explains
item.description: In the right circumstances, job hopping can actually be beneficial for your career and bank account. Jill Schlesinger explains why.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Manhattan DA urges NYC's low-income workers to report wage theft
item.description: The Economic Policy Institute estimates that workers lose more than $50 billion a year to wage theft. New York City is cracking down on the crime and other abuses of low-income workers.

item.title: Prince Harry must pay Daily Mail publisher millions after invasion of privacy case fails
item.description: Prince Harry and six others, including musician Elton John, must pay the publisher of Daily Mail millions of pounds after their failed invasion of privacy suit. Ian Lee has more details.

item.title: Cuban immigrant speaks out after deportation to one of the world's most dangerous countries
item.description: The U.S. Department of State has put Central African Republic under a "do not travel" advisory, citing unrest, crime, kidnapping and terrorism risks. Despite this, the Trump administration has deported immigrants from other counties there. Camilo Montoya-Galvez spoke with immigrants who were deported, as well as their families.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy "was frankly psychotic," psychiatrist recommends no criminal liability
item.description: Several medical experts testified in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy. Clancy admitted to killing her three children but claims she was experiencing postpartum psychosis. Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: Serena Williams, Carlos Alcaraz will play mixed doubles at the U.S. Open
item.description: Serena Williams will team up with Carlos Alcaraz to create a powerhouse mixed doubles pair in her return to the U.S. Open.

item.title: Russian and Ukrainian attacks kill at least 10 after deadly mall drone strike
item.description: The attacks come a day after a two-wave drone strike on a shopping mall in Zelenskyy's hometown killed 16 people.

item.title: Trump's trade deal with Canada collapses
item.description: The U.S. plans to impose 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian products after negotiations between the two countries failed. The Canadian prime minister said he would match the tariffs "dollar for dollar." Olivia Rinaldi has more.

item.title: Sword attack at school in Sweden kills 17-year-old girl, officials say
item.description: An 18-year-old with a sword attacked a school on Friday in central Sweden, killing a 17-year-old girl and seriously injuring at least two others.

item.title: Supreme Court temporarily allows work on White House ballroom to continue
item.description: Chief Justice John Roberts issued a stay that will remain in place until the Supreme Court takes further action.

item.title: European wildfires expose, detonate buried explosives from past wars
item.description: The wildfires burning across Europe this summer have revealed World War I and II ordnance lurking beneath the blackened landscape.

item.title: How a teen found "a sense of control" as she fought cancer
item.description: Alayna Riozzi-Bodine was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma the summer before her senior year of high school.

item.title: The Uplift: The Shatners
item.description: William Sahtner and his daughter Melanie Shatner-Gretsch open up about their individual cancer battles that led to a strengthened bond between them. Plus, more heartwarming news

item.title: Drastic water cuts issued for California, Nevada and Arizona from Colorado River
item.description: Federal officials announced sharp water cuts for the next two years on Friday for three Western states that rely on the imperiled Colorado River.

item.title: Reports of sexual assault in U.S. military declined for third straight year
item.description: The review included data from an anonymous survey conducted every other year that asks service members whether they've been the victim of unwanted sexual conduct or harassment.

item.title: Alfalfa sprouts recalled after E. coli, salmonella outbreak sickens dozens
item.description: An outbreak of E. coli and salmonella that has sickened dozens of people across 15 states has been linked to an alfalfa grower in Minnesota, federal health officials said Friday.

item.title: Nearly 25% of workers are "functionally unemployed," analysis finds
item.description: An alternative measure of unemployment that accounts for wages suggests the U.S. labor market is weaker than it looks.

item.title: People are scrambling to find wads of cash dropped all over American cities
item.description: Cash drop social media accounts have people racing to find money hidden across the country. Here's what's behind the viral videos.

item.title: Woman covertly filmed by Meta smart glasses raises privacy concerns
item.description: One woman is speaking out after she was secretly filmed, saying that technology like Meta's AI-powered smart glasses threatens personal privacy.

item.title: AI companies accused of hoarding and destroying millions of books
item.description: Consumer advocates are urging the FTC to examine whether AI developers are hurting competition and reducing public access to source material.
